result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

MEMO - March 2026 US accruals for services received but not yet billed
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com (senior accountant) | Date: 2026-04-03 | Entity: Halvard Systems Inc. (US, USD)

1. SCOPE AND APPROACH
Per Accounting Policy Manual s.5, expenses are recorded in the period the goods/services are received; services received but not invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the best available evidence. I searched the document store for US evidence of March services not yet invoiced (timesheets, vendor confirmations, engagement terms) and compared March US vendor bills against the January/February recurring-vendor population to identify gaps.

2. ENTRIES POSTED (both dated 2026-03-31, period 2026-03)

a) JE-00304 - USD 7,350.00 - POSTED (within posting authority)
   DR 6520 Consulting Fees        7,350.00
   CR 2100 Accrued Expenses       7,350.00
   Juniper Data Consulting, March data-warehouse modelling. 42.0 hours approved by M. Osei (Head of Data) on 2026-03-31 x USD 175.00/hr per SOW 2026-02 = USD 7,350.00. Billed monthly in arrears; invoice issues in April.
   Support attached: DOC-0204 (approved March timesheet), DOC-0074 (SOW 2026-02).

b) JE-00305 - USD 14,250.00 - POSTED, PENDING CONTROLLER APPROVAL
   DR 6500 Legal Fees            14,250.00
   CR 2100 Accrued Expenses      14,250.00
   Parker & Rowe LLP, time recorded on Halvard matters through 2026-03-31 (28.5 hours, Series B side-letter review), per vendor billing confirmation dated 2026-04-01; invoice to issue 2026-04-10.
   Support attached: DOC-0209.
   Approval: exceeds the USD 10,000 per-entry senior accountant authority (Policy s.1), so request_approval was submitted to the Controller immediately after posting. The entry remains pending until approved.

Total March US accrual: USD 21,600.00 credited to 2100. No entries were split to avoid the approval threshold - these are two unrelated vendors/transactions.

3. ITEMS CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT ACCRUED
- Brightline Media, USD 11,000.00 (DOC-0197, dated 2026-03-27): a quote/proposal for an April product-launch campaign, work to start 2026-04-06 on signature. No service was received in March and there is no signed commitment, so it is not a March liability (Policy s.5: quotes and proposals are not liabilities). Excluded.
- All recurring US vendors (Lumen Office Leasing, Stackline Cloud, Quire Docs, Tessellate BI, Con Edison, Oakridge Creative) issued March invoices (DOC-0144, 0161, 0162, 0165, 0167, 0168), so no "missing invoice" accrual is required for them; those sit in AP, not 2100. Figtree Software is an annual prepaid license (DOC-0024), amortized, not accrued.

4. OTHER OBSERVATIONS FOR THE CONTROLLER
- Account 2100 had no activity before these entries; its USD 38,200.00 credit balance is entirely from the 2026-01-01 opening-balance migration (JE-00013). That legacy balance has no supporting detail in the document store and should be substantiated/rolled forward separately - I did not adjust it (Policy s.11: no plugs).
- Juniper's SOW is effective 2026-02-01, but there is no February timesheet, invoice, or accrual on record and accounts 6520/6500 had no activity prior to these entries. If February hours were worked, the February charge is currently unrecorded; February is closed, so any true-up would land in March/April once the April invoice arrives. I did not accrue an amount for February because no evidence of February hours exists.
- Classification note: the Parker & Rowe fees relate to a Series B side-letter review. Legal costs directly attributable to an equity issuance are often charged against 3100 Additional Paid-in Capital rather than expense. I recorded them to 6500 Legal Fees in the absence of policy guidance and pending confirmation that the Series B closes; please redirect if you prefer APIC treatment.
- Both accruals should be reversed in April when the Juniper and Parker & Rowe invoices are received and booked to AP.

5. CHECKLIST
US "AP cutoff review" set to in_progress - the unbilled-services accrual portion is complete; the remaining bill-to-ledger cutoff testing is outstanding. No exceptions were flagged for this task: every accrual posted is fully supported and the one excluded item (Brightline) is correctly a non-liability rather than an unsupportable one.
